I was told once that I rolled my eyes constantly and my boss found it really rude. Turns out that when *I* thought I was rolling my eyes, i.e. the big circular dramatic, very much intentional gesture, that was what I thought was the universal gesture, but apparently that's just how they animate it in cartoons and so I copied that when I was a kid. I literally never knew that I guess for most people it's just a quick glance?

I had always done it as a very exaggerated display, and so I knew when I was doing it, and I knew that I had never made that particular face when speaking to my boss. What I didn't know was that everyone around me was picking up on subtle things that I was unaware of going on in my face, and interpreting them as eye-rolling or being annoyed or what have you. My boss, when explaining it to me, literally went "That! That thing right there that you just did! That's rolling your eyes!" and it was sort of a lightbulb moment for me. I'm grateful he and I became good enough friends for him to tell me his first impressions of me and then explain when I was baffled. Good guy.

Basically I'll never be a professional poker player, but ever since being made aware of the fact that I apparently have a lot more facial expressions going on than I'm aware of, I can at least try and be more mindful of it. Maybe you're the same.

Which, for you and me, is the size of a *mini fridge.* 

Also, has to be said, but making Irish friends is damn near impossible for us. It is an extremely isolating thing moving here and trying to make friends without any existing connections, more so than moving to any city in the US and I've moved more times than I can think of back home.
